To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) personal effort in social networks is age-differentially related to emotional closening and perceptions of reciprocy, (ii) perceived effort in social relationships increases with age and is associated with more conflict, and (iii) the findings are similar across different family-life contexts (i.e., biological parents, parents from stepfamilies with at least one biological and one stepchild, and childless individuals).
